What each component can be set to, for a network

Source: R/mira_options.R
mira_options.Rd

Lists the attributes a network offers to each component's arguments: the columns and computed attributes color_by and size_by take, the columns conditions in mira_filter() and mira_mode_meta(layers = ) can use, and the measures of the meta-network. For each, the type MiRA gives it and a summary of its values, to choose a mapping and write color_values before making the plot.

Usage

mira_options(net, ...)

Arguments

net

A multilayer network from emln (as for mira()).

...

Arguments of mira(): bipartite, setA_type, directed, directed_interlayer.

Value

A data frame of class mira_options, one row per argument and attribute, with columns component, argument, attribute, type, switchable, source ("node", "state node", "link", "layer", "computed" by MiRA, or "keyword"), sets (on a bipartite network, the node sets that have the attribute) and values. It prints grouped by component, with MiRA's computed node attributes on one line (the data frame has a row for each), and with the sets only when they differ between attributes. Filter it as a data frame, keeping all its columns: rows chosen with opts[opts$argument == "size_by", ] print as the table does; for some columns only, use as.data.frame(opts).

Details

Columns MiRA does not offer are left out (the ones that identify rows, weight, the coordinates; see mira_node()). The node type column is listed as node_type, MiRA's name for it, whatever it is called in net$nodes; conditions in mira_filter() use the name in the data.

Give the same arguments as to mira(): they decide what MiRA computes (in- and out-degree only on a directed network) and whether nodes can be set per set (bipartite = TRUE).

Types. "categorical" (one color per value) or "continuous" (a gradient) is the scale MiRA picks by default: numbers with more than two values, or with a name such as abundance or degree, are continuous, unless the name marks groups (module, cluster); text is categorical. Where switchable is TRUE, color_scale can choose the other one (see mira_scales). The type also decides the palettes color_palette can name: categorical ones ("Okabe-Ito", "Set1", ...) or continuous ones ("magma", "RdBu", ...). "set" and "individual" are keywords: one color per node set, one color per layer. Columns for conditions have the type of their values: "number", "text" or "logical".

See also

mira() to start a plot; mira_node() and the other components for the arguments; mira_scales for color_values, color_scale, color_palette, color_reverse and color_limits.

Examples

library(emln)
net <- load_emln(17) # 4 layers; bird and plant nodes
#> Creating state node map
#> Creating extended link list with node IDs

mira_options(net, bipartite = TRUE, setA_type = "bird")
